what_i_see: Large, roughly round, smooth low-surface-brightness patch ~12" across, with fairly defined edges and no nucleus; a spiral galaxy lies ~11" N. Only VIS data here: the colour panel is pure blue (no NISP), so colour is uninformative.
most_likely: A low-surface-brightness dwarf galaxy, or an optical ghost/scattered-light feature in VIS.
against_it: Round, smooth, sharp-edged shape and no catalogue counterpart fit a ghost; Legacy DR10 cutout shows nothing (inconclusive, shallower).
decisive_test: Inspect individual VIS exposures and later NISP coverage: a ghost shifts between dithers or is absent; a dwarf stays fixed.
catalogue_notes: No SIMBAD, NED, or Gaia source within 30". Nearest bright star 2MASS J04465649-5113146 (G=12.8, high proper motion) at 86". No DR8 photo-z rows within 12" (likely coverage gap). No match in Jacobs+2019, Huang+2020/2021 (cone 10"; Rojas+2022 query unvalidated).
